Subject: POC scope & model prioritization — LumenPay trial

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an agreed starting point for the POC kickoff. I captured items we discussed and added a recommended model prioritization based on your latency/cost targets and multilingual needs.

Call highlights (short):
- Goal: Replace rule-based support routing and improve triage accuracy for EN/FR/DE/ES.
- Target latency: p50 < 450ms for short queries; p95 < 900ms.
- Budget guideline: ~€0.01–€0.03 per 1k tokens during POC.
- Data: No customer PII in initial test; will validate data residency requirement for later stages.

Recommended model prioritization for the trial:
1) Primary: Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized FP16) — best mix of instruction-following and latency for EU region.
2) Secondary (fallback): Redwood-2.7B-int8 — lower cost, slightly higher error rate on complex multi-step prompts.
3) Gatekeeper/expand: Mistral-22B (hosted canary) — only for final acceptance A/B if you want to compare quality for hard intent cases.

Multilingual approach:
- Baseline: single-model inference with Mistral-7B (it handled EN/FR/DE/ES in our internal eval).
- Fallback policy: route non-EN to the same model but use locale-specific prompt templates; if quality < threshold, fallback to locale-specific small finetune (outside POC).

POC success criteria (proposal):
- Functional: intent classification accuracy >= 85% on the provided eval set (EN/FR/DE/ES combined).
- Latency: p95 tokens generation < 900ms for 32-token responses under expected load.
- Ops: automated rollback to fallback model if p95 latency > 1.2s for >2 minutes.
- Business: 20% reduction in routing false positives vs baseline rules.

Evaluation plan & timeline (fast 3-week sprint):
Week 0 (this week): confirm data subset & acceptance rubric — owners: LumenPay (Aisha) + Redwood (Aditya).
Week 1: baseline runs + automated eval harness over 2k test prompts (owner: Aditya).
Week 2: tuning (prompt templates, batching) + integration smoke (owner: LumenPay + Redwood infra).
Week 3: acceptance run and demo (owner: Ben) — acceptance decision and next-phase options.

Ownership matrix (POC):
- Redwood infra & model config: Aditya Rao
- Sales & success contact / commercial: Ben Carter
- POC sponsor / acceptance: Aisha Khan (LumenPay)

Attachments: I attached a slim success criteria spreadsheet and a first-pass model matrix (CSV) with perf/cost estimates.

Next steps I propose now:
1) Aisha: confirm the eval subset and whether FR/DE/ES samples are available by Tuesday (2028-11-06).
2) Aditya: provision EU-hosted Mistral-7B quantized instance + fallback slot.
3) Ben: schedule the kickoff call for Monday next week (30 mins).

If that all sounds good I’ll file the HubSpot deal update and create the Drive folder for artifacts.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Couple of pragmatic suggestions from my side: 
- Add an automated traffic-throttling policy that switches traffic to the smaller fallback model when queue depth > 8 for > 30s. That keeps the p95 SLO stable.
- For multilingual checks include a small adversarial prompt set (10-20 examples per locale) to capture hallucination/regression cases early.

If we do the A/B to Mistral-22B, keep it read-only (no routing to production actions) — we only want quality signals.

-Rishi
